contractor_underwriting: Came back clean, against expectation. Total provisions GBP9.9m on GBP1,045.7m revenue (rectification GBP3.5m on an insured water-treatment claim with a GBP4.3m insurance recovery asset, work completing 2026; other GBP6.4m dilapidations and a fire-safety claim). No onerous-contract provision recognised. A465 and Peterborough/Kings Dyke appear nowhere in AR2025 - resolved. Crucially the fixed-price premise is REFUTED for the current book: the GBP7.0bn forward work 'included no single-stage lump sum contracts' and is 'predominantly long-term programmes of work with target cost contracts'. Cash conversion 113% of reported operating profit (108% adjusted); contract liabilities fell GBP32.7m while cash still rose.
order_book: Forward work GBP7.0bn at FY25 (+30% vs GBP5.4bn), ~7x revenue: order book GBP3.6bn + preferred bidder GBP3.4bn; GBP1.1bn covers 90% of FY26 forecast revenue. But at the 14-May-26 AGM update the book was only 'broadly consistent with the GBP7bn FY25 year end position' - flat through H1-26. AMP8 confirmed tailwind (United Utilities raised its AMP8 programme GBP2.5bn / +30% to GBP11.5bn; Thames Water live across nine sites). HS2 confirmed headwind already taken (FY25 rail revenue fell on a revised HS2 schedule moving work into FY26+). RIS3 confirmed at GBP27bn over five years. Customer mix improved to 51% private/regulated from 30% two years ago.
edge_explainer: The screen ranked Costain on net cash (29% of cap) and an 8.6% FCF yield, not on book. Primary verification confirms the business is real and improved - no debt, a clean provisions book, a target-cost rather than lump-sum contract mix, 113% cash conversion, and a GBP7bn forward book into an accelerating UK infrastructure cycle. What the screen cannot see is that there is no de-rate here to buy. The price is 3.2% from its 52-week high after a 68.7% twelve-month run, and the EV/EBIT multiple has expanded from 1.3x at Dec-2023 to 8.9x today - a five-year high, not a discount to its own history - while the near-term margin guide steps back from 4.5% to ~4.0% and the promised step change is deferred to FY27. Two screen defects fire and both cut the same way: the GBP60.0m pension surplus inflates book equity, taking P/B from 2.18x to 2.84x once stripped, and it is recoverable only on wind-up (refund basis, then a 25% UK charge, against buy-out pricing that would likely consume most of it); and the period-end net cash of GBP189.3m sits 24% above the filer's own average month-end figure of GBP152.6m, which lifts EV/EBIT from 8.92x to 9.71x. Expected fair value of ~249p against 211p is roughly a 12%/yr return with a fat contractor left tail and a pension scheme the size of the market cap running a levered LDI book - fairly-paid risk, not edge. Frame-reject.
